# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.

# Repository Exploration Report: /app (Transaction Enrichment / Categorization Service)

## 1. Overall Structure

The repo is a single Python Flask microservice for enriching Indian bank statement transactions. Single commit (`047782b import codebase`), branch `main`.

```
/app
├── .gitignore                     (ignores *.csv, __pycache__, TEST*.xml, etc.)
├── Dockerfile                     (python:3.9.2, gunicorn on port 9898, `pip3 install -e .`)
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                   (Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4, fuzzywuzzy, python-Levenshtein, scipy, scikit-learn)
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py            (Flask app factory + request timing hooks; lines 7, 15-24)
        ├── Controller.py          (936 lines - Flask routes / orchestration)
        ├── BankScripts/           (35 per-bank categorization modules)
        │   Andhra.py, AuSmallFinanceBank.py, Axis.py, BOB.py, BOI.py, Bandhan.py,
        │   BankOfMaharashtra.py, Canara.py, Central.py, Citi.py, CityUnion.py, DCB.py,
        │   Federal.py, HDFC.py, ICICI.py, IDBI.py, IDFC.py, Indian.py, Indusind.py,
        │   Karnataka.py, KarurVyasa.py, Kotak.py, PNB.py, Paytm.py, RBL.py, SBI.py,
        │   SVC.py, Saraswat.py, SouthIndian.py, StandardCharted.py, Syndicate.py,
        │   TamilnadMerchantile.py, UCO.py, UnionBank.py, YES.py
        └── UtilityScripts/        (cross-bank enrichment stages + regex dictionaries)
            AppUtil.py, RegexConstants.py, BankRegexConstants.py,
            Purpose.py, CleanName.py, CardPurpose.py, CardCleanNames.py,
            InternalPayment.py, SalaryDetection.py, PFMCategorization.py,
            SimpleDescription.py, RecurrentTxns.py,
            TransactionCategoryEnums.py, TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py
```

### Entry points / pipeline (Controller.py)
- `home()` — `/` health check (line 51-53).
- `recurrentTransactions()` — `POST /recurrentTransactions` (lines 55-67) → `recurrent_transactions()`.
- `categorizeTransaction()` — `POST /categorizeTransaction` (lines 69-936). Takes `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, `transactions[]`; normalizes to a pandas DataFrame via `AppUtil.clean_input_df()` (line 87), then dispatches on `bank` through a giant if/elif chain (lines 91-931, one nearly-identical block per bank). Each block runs the same pipeline:
  1. `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` — per-bank category + partyName extraction (BankScripts/).
  2. If `CREDIT_CARD`: `card_clean_names()` + `card_purpose()`.
  3. `purpose(transactions, accountType)` — subcategory/merchantType (UtilityScripts/Purpose.py).
  4. `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` — merchant name normalization (UtilityScripts/CleanName.py).
  5. `internal_payment(...)` if accountHolder present.
  6. `salary_detection(...)` if SAVING.
  7. `pfm_categorization()` + `simple_description()` if `isPFMEnabled`.

All logic is vectorized pandas: lists of `[condition_mask, choice]` pairs fed to `np.select(...)` — first matching rule wins.

## 2. Transaction Categorization (category from narration text)

Category assignment (CHEQUE_PAID / CHEQUE_DEPOSIT / UPI / NEFT / IMPS / RTGS / ATM_WITHDRAWAL / CASH_DEPOSIT / AUTO_PAYMENT / REVERSAL / charges, default **TRANSFER**) happens in the **BankScripts** modules — one `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` function per file. Each builds a `conditions_choices` list of regex tests on `transactions.description` combined with `transactions.type` (`DEBIT`/`CREDIT`) and amount conditions, then:

```python
transactions['transactionCategory'] = np.select(df['conditions'], df['choices'], default="TRANSFER")
```

Representative files (all follow this pattern):

- **SBI** — `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/SBI.py`, `categorize_SBI_transactions()` line 8.
  - Category rules: lines 10-70. E.g. cheque: line 45 `"\\bCLG\\b|^BY CLEARING|^TO CLEARING|\\bCHQ\\b|CHEQUE|CHEQ NO"` + DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID`; line 46 same + CREDIT → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`; UPI line 50; IMPS line 54; NEFT line 55; RTGS line 56; ATM line 43; CASH_DEPOSIT line 63.
  - Subcategory overrides: lines 76-88 (INVESTMENT, SALARY via `\\bSAL[0-9]+`, etc.).
- **HDFC** — `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py`, `categorize_HDFC_transactions()` line 9.
  - Category rules: lines 11-104. Cheque: lines 69-75 (`CHQ DEP RET`, `Chq Paid|CHQ COLL|CHEQ PAID` → CHEQUE_PAID line 74; `CHQ DEP|CHQ COLL` + CREDIT → CHEQUE_DEPOSIT line 75); UPI line 58 (`^UPI|UPI-?\s?`); IMPS line 59; NEFT line 60; ATM line 49; payment-gateway categories lines 78-87; duplicate debit/credit heuristics (reversal/bounce) lines 98-99.
  - Subcategory: lines 112-132 (LOAN, INVESTMENT, SALARY, INTERNAL_PAYMENT via `\\bSELF\\b` line 127).
- Other banks: Kotak.py lines 64-66 (MICR/CLG cheque rules), BOB.py lines 68-69, BankOfMaharashtra.py line 65, Citi.py line 30, etc. Every BankScripts/*.py has the same shape; sizes range 68-327 lines (Kotak largest at 327).

Second-pass, bank-agnostic categorization:
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py`** — `purpose(transactions, accountType)` line 9. Assigns `transactionSubcategory` (lines 12-152: SALARY, LOAN, LOAN_REPAYMENT, INSURANCE, INVESTMENT, RENT, FUEL, TRAVEL, EDUCATION, UTILITY_BILL, E_COMMERCE, etc.), overrides `transactionCategory` (lines 154-170: TDS, TAX_REFUND, CASHBACK, REFUND, DIRECT_TAX/INDIRECT_TAX, FIXED_DEPOSIT, INTEREST), assigns `merchantType` (lines 182-278: NBFC, HFC, Flight, Gaming, Electricity, Mutual Fund, Pharmacy, ...), then cleanups (lines 280-298).
- **CardPurpose.py** (`card_purpose()` line 9) — same, for credit-card accounts.
- **PFMCategorization.py** (`pfm_categorization()` line 8) — maps to PFM buckets `pfmCategoryOne` (line 81), `pfmCategoryTwo` (line 191), `pfmCategoryType` (line 204).
- **Enums**: TransactionCategoryEnums.py (`TransactionCategory` enum, line 3, 170 lines) and TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py (`TransactionSubcategory`, 135 lines) hold display names used by SimpleDescription.py (`simple_description()` line 6, builds `pfmSimpleDescription` line 17).

### Regex dictionaries used by categorization
- **`UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py`** (191 lines) — bank-agnostic keyword regexes: `SALARY` (line 6), `LOAN_REP` (line 9), `LOAN` (line 13), `CREDIT_CARD` (line 20), `SHOPPING` (21), `TRAVEL` (48), `UTILITY` (61), `INSURANCE` (64), `INVEST` (66), `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` (86), `INSUFF_BOUNCE` (87), `INTERNAL_PAY` (93), merchantType lists `NBFC` (105), `HFC` (107), `INSTANT_LOAN` (108), `PAYMENT_GATEWAY` (188), etc.
- **`UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py`** (432 lines) — per-bank patterns (see next section).

## 3. Counterparty Name Extraction (partyName)

Two layers:

### Layer A: raw extraction inside each BankScripts module
After category assignment, each bank script builds `transactions['partyName']` (and `party2` = partyName without spaces) using tokenizer helpers and regex extraction, keyed off the derived category.

Helpers in **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py`**:
- `sep_by_(description, n1, n2)` line 14 (split on `/`), `sep_by_dash` line 17, `sep_by_wave` line 20, `sep_by_star` line 23, `sep_by_comma` line 26, `sep_by_colon` line 29, `sep_by_under` line 32, bracket variants lines 35-45.
- `py_extract(description, pat, index)` line 61 — regex `.str.extract` with NaN handling.
- `fuzzy_match(s1, s2, dist)` line 48 — fuzzywuzzy ratio (used by internal-payment detection).

Examples:
- **SBI.py** partyName extraction: lines 97-161 (first pass; e.g. UPI → `sep_by_(description,3,4)` line 99, NEFT → `sep_by_star(...,3,4)` line 122, IMPS via `SBI_IMPS_1/2/3` lines 149-151, card payments via `SBI_CP_PATTERN*`); second-pass cleanup lines 163-190 (strip `LOCATION_CLEAN`, `TRF_STOP_WORDS` from BankRegexConstants.py lines 64-65); `party2` created line 192.
- **HDFC.py** partyName extraction: lines 146-221.
  - NEFT/IMPS: lines 155-162 (e.g. `^IMPS-|^NEFT [CD][Rr]` → `sep_by_dash(description,2,3)` line 159 — 3rd dash-token is the beneficiary name); UPI: lines 149-154 (`^UPI-` → `sep_by_dash(...,1,2)` line 154); Razorpay/gateway special cases lines 152-153, 155-156, 176-179.
  - **Cheque, incl. your example "CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR"**: line 163 — `transactions.description.str.contains("CHQ PAID-", ...)` → `sep_by_dash(transactions.description,3,4)`; plus `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1..10` at lines 188-197 (patterns defined in BankRegexConstants.py lines 81-90, e.g. `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN6 = "Chq Paid-MICR CTS|CHQ PAID-MICR CTS"` → `sep_by_dash(...,3,4)` line 193).
  - Auto-pay/ACH names lines 169-174; fund-transfer patterns `HDFC_FT_PATTERN1-7`, `FT_PATTERN8-11` lines 202-213; salary-narration stop-word stripping lines 141-144, 217, 234-235; HDFC-specific cleanup lines 250-265 (`HDFC_CLEAN1`, drops `Micr Clg|Chq Paid` residue at line 260); `party2` line 275.

Per-bank extraction regexes live in **`UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py`**: SBI card/INB/IMPS/autopay patterns lines 8-62; HDFC POS/SI/cheque/FT lines 76-106; Union Bank NEFT/RTGS lines 120-129; PNB cheque/RTGS/transfer lines 140-159; Kotak billpay/IMPS/NEFT/RTGS/OS lines 171-231; generic FT/FT_CHQ patterns lines 241-298; IB patterns lines 302-311; cheque `CHQ_PATTERN1-4` + bank-name strip list `CHQ_CLEAN_KOTAK` lines 314-318; UCO cheque lines 380-383; bank-name removal lists `REMOVE_BANK_CB` line 417, `REMOVE_BANK_CITI` line 424, `CHQ_CLEAN_SCB` line 432.

### Layer B: canonical merchant-name normalization
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py`** (1971 lines) — `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` line 9. One enormous `conditions_choices` list mapping raw partyName/party2/description regexes to canonical merchant names ("DMart", "Dream11", "Google Play", "Tata Power", "RBL Bank", ...), organized by commented sections: DTH (13-26), internet (29-50), electricity (53-120), gas (123-130), entertainment/gaming (133-258), general expenses (261+), banks (~1730-1792), neobanks (1794), etc. Final selects: partyName line 1944, `party2` rebuild line 1946, merchantType overrides lines 1948-1956, subcategory overrides lines 1958-1967. Bank-specific branches, e.g. SBI pension line 1185, SBI defence-accounts line 1208, IDBI INET line 1939.
- **CardCleanNames.py** (927 lines) — `card_clean_names(transactions)` line 9; same idea for credit-card descriptions (final select line 926).
- **InternalPayment.py** — `internal_payment()` line 8: fuzzy-matches extracted `partyName` against the account holder (stop-word stripping line 10, `fuzzy_match` threshold 75 at lines 22/39) to tag `INTERNAL_PAYMENT` and set `isInternalPayment` (line 60).
- **SalaryDetection.py** — `salary_detection()` line 16: clusters `party2` names using Levenshtein distance + `scipy` hierarchical clustering (`cut_tree(linkage(...), height=1.5)` line 34) to detect salary/second-salary/reimbursement credits.
- **RecurrentTxns.py** — `recurrent_transactions()` line 8: same clustering to assign `Group_ID` for recurring-transaction grouping.

## 4. Test Fixtures / Baseline Corpus / How Tests Are Run

**There are none in this repository.** Verified thoroughly:
- Only 54 tracked files; no `tests/`, no `test_*.py`, no pytest/tox/CI config, no fixture CSV/JSON/txt anywhere under /app (search for `*fixture*`, `*corpus*`, `*baseline*`, `*.csv`, `*.json` returned nothing outside `.git`).
- `.gitignore` line 52 ignores `*.csv` and line 30 `TEST*.xml`, hinting fixtures/corpora and JUnit-style reports existed in the original environment but were deliberately excluded from version control.
- The only testing-related artifacts are commented-out dendrogram debug code marked "For testing purpose only" in SalaryDetection.py lines 27-32 and RecurrentTxns.py lines 16-21.
- Practical verification path today is black-box: run the Flask app (`pip3 install -e categorizationapp && gunicorn categorizationapp:app`, port 9898 per Dockerfile) and POST payloads to `/categorizeTransaction` with `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, and a `transactions` array (fields used: `description`, `type`, `amount`, `balanceAfterTransaction`, `remark`, `transactionDate`).

## Key Takeaways

- Categorization = per-bank regex rule tables in `BankScripts/<Bank>.py` (`categorize_*_transactions`), first-match `np.select`, default `TRANSFER`; refined by `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` and `PFMCategorization.py`.
- Name extraction = same bank scripts (delimiter slicing via `AppUtil.sep_by_*` + `py_extract` with patterns from `BankRegexConstants.py`), then canonicalization in `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` (savings/current) or `CardCleanNames.py` (credit cards).
- The example narration `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` is HDFC-style: category via HDFC.py line 74 (`Chq Paid` + DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID`), name via HDFC.py line 163 (`CHQ PAID-` → 4th dash-token) and `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN*` rules (HDFC.py lines 188-197 / BankRegexConstants.py lines 81-90).
- No automated tests or fixture corpus exist in the repo; `.gitignore` suggests CSV corpora were kept out of git.

import pandas as pd

def run(bankfunc, rows, acct="SAVING"):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    if 'remark' not in df: df['remark'] = ""
    if 'balanceAfterTransaction' not in df: df['balanceAfterTransaction'] = 1000.0
    df['amount'] = pd.to_numeric(df['amount'])
    out = bankfunc(df.copy(), acct)
    return out[['description','type','amount','transactionCategory','partyName']]

steps.message:
All five RC 2.14 findings are resolved. Summary of the changes:

**F-1 — bare cheque-number note → generic transfer** (`BankScripts/PNB.py:60`)
The debit-side cheque rule only accepted a 5-digit remark (`^[0-9]{5}$`) while its credit twin on the next line accepts `^[0-9]{5,6}$`, so a standard 6-digit cheque number fell through to `TRANSFER`. Widened the debit rule to `{5,6}`. 5-digit notes and every keyword-shaped cheque note were already correct and are unchanged.

**F-2 — `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` → counterparty "Micr Clg"** (`BankScripts/AuSmallFinanceBank.py:78`, `BankScripts/Canara.py:165`)
The generic `^CHQ PAID-` rule takes dash-token 1, which for this 3-token layout is the internal clearing tag. Added a narrower rule for the `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-<NAME>` layout (dash-token 2, mirroring Canara's existing `Chq Paid-Home Clearing-` rule) ahead of the generic one. Two-token `CHQ PAID-<NAME>` and `<NAME>-Chq Paid` layouts keep their current extraction.

**F-3 — plain NEFT credits with blank counterparty** (`BankScripts/PNB.py:110`)
`py_extract(pat="NEFT (.*)", index=1)` requested capture group 1 from a pattern that has only one group, so it always returned an empty series — every plain `NEFT …` narration got a blank name. Restored `index=0` (the only group). All other NEFT layouts route through earlier, unmodified rules.

**F-4 — P2P IMPS credit showing the bare reference number** (`BankScripts/Syndicate.py:69`, `BankScripts/Bandhan.py:61`)
For `IMPS:<ref>:<name>` (Syndicate) and `IMPS/P2A/<ref>/<name>` (Bandhan) the generic rules picked the token holding the 12-digit RRN, and neither bank blanks numeric names downstream — so the reference surfaced as the sender. Added narrow, ref-anchored rules (`^IMPS:[0-9]+:` → colon-token 2; `IMPS/P2A/[0-9]+/` → slash-token 3) before the generic ones. These preconditions only match rows where the current output is the numeric ref, so any narration currently resolving a name is untouched (verified: `IMPS:<name>`, `IMPS/<ref>/<name>`, `IMPS<name>` styles unchanged).

**F-5 — ₹1 account-verification credit filed as transfer** (`BankScripts/Canara.py:19`)
`amount.lt(1)` can never match the standard ₹1 penny-drop, so those credits defaulted to `TRANSFER`. Changed to `amount.lt(2)` (the convention HDFC/PNB/RBL use). This strictly widens the match, so every fixture that currently classifies as `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` still does, and ordinary deposits (≥ ₹2) are unaffected.

Each fix was verified against the finding's fixture shape plus neighbouring layouts and ordinary traffic through all five edited scripts (categories and names reproduce exactly as before), and the full app plus all 35 bank scripts still import cleanly.
